children: How much Shein would have had to pay early investors if it hadn't launched an IPO by the end of the year.
The fast-fashion brand pressed ahead with its plans to go public despite slowing growth and regulatory headwinds in the U.S. and Europe. Its stock ended its first trading day 0.12% lower today.
While the more-than-$4 billion liability will now be off its books, Shein said it was saddled with another bill: the roughly $3.5 billion it owed its early investors upon going public.
